label: Real Historical Data
description: Interactive planning on past seasons with the frozen real-data pipeline: OSI SAF sea ice and the frozen U-Net forecast, daily ERA5 winds and CMEMS reanalysis currents, weekly USNIC iceberg lists with the calibrated drift ensemble, and risk-budgeted routing. Nothing is fitted or tuned. Research / decision-support only; not a certified navigation product.

hindsight_forcing: Hindsight forcing: for every day after the issue date, winds (ERA5) and currents (CMEMS reanalysis) are reanalysis fields that were only known afterwards, not forecasts. Iceberg drift and current-aided ship speed are therefore more favourable than a live forecast would allow. Sea ice uses only observations up to the issue date.
limitations: Research / decision-support prototype; not certified for navigation or safety-critical operational use.
The sea-ice forecast does not beat persistence in a statistically trusted way: trust horizon 0 days against persistence (21 days against damped persistence and climatology).
Iceberg drift is only slightly better than assuming no movement on position; its demonstrated value is probabilistic (coverage near nominal), confirmed on 5-6 tracks in 2024-25.
The vessel is a generic polar research vessel and its ice class is a placeholder (REPLACE_WITH_VERIFIED_CLASS); fuel is an index, not tonnes.
Iceberg positions come from the latest weekly USNIC list on or before the issue date (up to 14 days old); drift starts from that position at the issue date. Only large tracked icebergs are included.
Replans assume the day's sea-ice analysis is in hand that day; operational product latency is not modelled.

forecast_mode.label: Forecast / hackathon estimate
forecast_mode.disclosure: Forecast estimate: future-year Antarctic observations/forcing are not fully available in this demo runtime. Results use the latest available real seasonal data and explicitly labelled proxy/estimated forcing where required. This is a research/hackathon estimate, not a certified navigation route.
forecast_mode.method: Dates after the real archive are planned with the unchanged real-data engine from an analogue start: the same calendar day in the latest archive season that covers the run. Sea ice: that day's real OSI SAF observations (proxy starting state, not an observation of the requested year) forecast with the frozen U-Net. Winds and currents: ERA5/CMEMS reanalysis of the analogue days (proxy forcing, not a forecast). Icebergs: the latest official USNIC list on or before the requested date, positions held from the list date, then drifted with the calibrated ensemble. Engine dates map one-to-one onto the requested dates by a fixed day offset.

seasonal_analogue.label: Historical seasonal analogue
seasonal_analogue.disclosure: Forecast / hackathon estimate from a historical seasonal analogue: no forecast exists for this date. Sea ice is the real observed ice of the same calendar days in earlier years, winds and currents are the ERA5/CMEMS reanalysis of the analogue date, and icebergs are the latest official USNIC list (or the analogue year's list when none is recent). This shows what those years would have meant for this route; it is not a meteorological or oceanographic forecast and not a certified navigation route.
seasonal_analogue.method: Dates after the real archive that the forecast pathway cannot serve are estimated without any model: the analogue date is the requested calendar day in the most recent earlier year with real sea ice, winds and currents for the whole run. Each sea-ice scenario is the real OSI SAF observation of the same calendar days in one of up to 7 earlier years (the analogue year itself excluded), shifted by -7..+7 days; winds and currents are the analogue date's ERA5/CMEMS reanalysis; icebergs are the latest official USNIC list when it is at most 120 days old (held, then drifted), else the official list of the analogue date (drifted). Engine dates map one-to-one onto the requested dates by a fixed day offset.
